facts.statement: Sample extract containing real patient data was sent by Harrington and forwarded to offshore engineers in Pune prior to BAA execution.
facts.quote: Kevin Brooks (their data eng manager) emailed a "sample extract" on 12 Sep so we could size the pipeline. Pranav opened it here and forwarded to Sneha and Vikram in Pune to start profiling. "It's real data I think — names, DOBs, some diagnosis codes."
facts.whyItMatters: Regulated patient data was received and transferred to offshore staff in Pune before the BAA and MSA were executed and without required subcontractor BAA coverage and client consent.

facts.statement: Daniel Ortiz is being engaged as a US-based freelance data engineer to meet US-only data restrictions.
facts.quote: Dhaval: the BAA says nobody outside the US touches patient data, so he's bringing in Daniel Ortiz, freelance data engineer in Austin.
facts.whyItMatters: The BAA restricts patient data access to US personnel, but Harrington's prior written consent to engage Daniel Ortiz as a subcontractor is missing.

facts.statement: Harrington BAA requires $5M cyber insurance coverage, which exceeds the current $1M policy.
facts.quote: Our cyber policy is $1M btw, Harrington BAA wants 5.
facts.whyItMatters: The draft BAA requires $5M in cyber insurance coverage, but the company's active policy limit is $1M.

facts.statement: Rebecca requires the MSA and BAA to be executed together by October 1.
facts.quote: Dhaval: Rebecca needs MSA + BAA by 1 Oct.
facts.whyItMatters: Sets the required deadline for completing review and execution of both Harrington agreements.

facts.statement: Harrington MSA is targeted for October 1 on client paper that client counsel considers non-negotiable.
facts.quote: C-023 (MSA): need by 1 Oct (Rebecca). their lawyers say template is non-negotiable. $210k
facts.whyItMatters: Counterparty counsel asserts the contract template is non-negotiable with a target date of October 1.
